entities.summary:
Colotes (b. 319 BCE, Lampsacus) was a philosopher or thinker of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Lampsacus. 


 Colotes was a prominent figure in the Hellenistic school of Stoicism, known for his writings on logic, epistemology, and ethics. His philosophical views were influenced by the ideas of Zeno of Citium, the founder of Stoicism. 


 Colotes' work on logic, in particular, emphasized the importance of reasoning, analysis, and the use of language in understanding the world. His treatise on the subject, titled 'On Logic,' is still studied by scholars today. 


 Colotes' legacy extends beyond his philosophical contributions, as his ideas about logic and epistemology influenced the development of Western philosophy, particularly in the areas of epistemology and the philosophy of language. His work also had an impact on the development of logic and reasoning in other fields, such as science and mathematics.
